say: Someone said AI can't come up with a brand new idea.
Someone replied: sure it can. Put every Steam game on a map, find the empty spots, and turn them back into ideas.
So I tested it. It worked, just not the way they said.
First, I downloaded every game's page from Steam, the biggest PC game store. All one hundred and ninety-five thousand.
Then an AI turned each game's description into a point on a map, so similar games land close together.
That's called an embedding.
Two zombie shooters? Neighbors. A farming game? Far away.
Here's the map. Every dot is a real Steam game, and genres form neighborhoods.
To score an idea, I put it on the map and look at its ten closest games.
The farther away they are, the more unusual the idea.
Can new wording fake a high score?
No. When the AI rewrote real games in totally new words, most landed near the originals.
Then I found empty spots on the map, far from every game.
For each one, an AI wrote a game idea and kept rewriting it to land there.
For comparison, I also just asked the same AI: give me game ideas nobody has made.
Surprise: the empty spots lost.
For a typical idea from just asking, about sixteen thousand Steam games were more unusual. For the empty spots, fifty-three thousand. Fewer is better.
Why? I'd searched a simplified map that mostly knows genre and style.
On the full map, empty spots only tied with just asking.
What won? Using the map as a compass.
The AI writes an idea, the map says which games it's too close to, and it moves away.
Now only about eighty Steam games were more unusual.
And a second map it never saw agreed.
Here's what came out.
Captain a village's church bell ringers in eighteen twenty.
Be the hidden prompter, whispering lines to actors who forgot them.
Perform a silent film's sound effects live.
Write the first great English dictionary before the money runs out.
But unusual isn't never made, so another AI searched the web for all sixteen ideas.
Ten turned up nothing similar, though most checks were quick.
Five had something close.
And one already existed: a Viking rowing rhythm game called Ragnarock.
So, can AI come up with a new idea?
With the map as its compass, its typical idea was more unusual than ninety-nine point nine percent of Steam.
The map didn't invent them. It just kept saying: that's been done.
